body.text: How does Adrasan differ from busier Kemer and Antalya?

Adrasan replaces high-rise all-inclusive resorts and loud beach clubs with family-run wooden bungalows, citrus orchards, and a curved two-kilometer bay backed by pine hills. Located roughly 13 km from Olympos and Çıralı, the village enforces low-density building limits, keeping evenings quiet and centered on simple seaside fish dinners rather than late-night entertainment.

Unlike Kemer or Antalya's Lara and Konyaaltı strips, Adrasan has no mega-resorts, shopping malls, or jet-ski corridors dominating the shoreline. Most accommodations sit either along the riverfront shaded by plane trees or a short walk behind the sandy-pebble beach. That slower rhythm appeals to travelers who want direct trail access to the Lycian Way, morning swims before excursion buses arrive, and easy day trips to nearby ancient Olympos and the Yanartaş (Chimaera) flames.
Is a private boat to Suluada worth it vs crowded shared boats?

A private boat charter to Suluada is worth the extra cost for couples, families, or small groups who want quiet swim stops and flexible timing. Shared boats carry 30 to 60 passengers on fixed mid-morning schedules, whereas private captains leave Adrasan harbor earlier, reach Suluada before tour buses unload, and adjust coves if wind picks up.

Suluada sits off the western Antalya coast and can only be reached by boat, with Adrasan Harbor acting as the closest departure point ([Suluada Travel Guide 2026](https://www.grandtransfers.com/en/blog/suluada-travel-guide-2026-turkeys-maldives-boat-tours-transfers)). Standard shared excursions run six to seven hours and stop at Suluada's pale pebble beaches, the freshwater spring, Love Cave (Aşk Mağarası), and nearby coastal coves. In July and August, dozens of double-decker boats anchor simultaneously at Suluada's main beach, turning the shoreline noisy by 11:00 AM.

body.text: Which months have calm morning seas?

Late May through June and September through mid-October deliver the calmest morning sea conditions around Adrasan and Suluada, paired with warm swimming temperatures and fewer excursion boats. July and August bring reliable sunshine but stronger afternoon thermal winds across the Cape Gelidonya channel, while November through April sees swells that cancel most daily crossings.

Because Suluada lies near the exposed tip of the Teke Peninsula, afternoon chop can build quickly after 1:30 PM even on clear summer days. Scheduling your boat departure by 08:30 or 09:00 AM gives you glassy water at Suluada's eastern and western beaches before returning to the sheltered coves closer to Adrasan after lunch.

items: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a wide-brimmed hat, and a lightweight UV shirt, as Suluada has no natural shade or beach umbrellas.
Pack water shoes for stepping onto smooth white pebbles and rocky cave ledges.
Carry a dry bag and a light windbreaker for the open-water crossing back around Cape Gelidonya.
Confirm in advance whether drinking water, soft drinks, and snorkeling masks are included in your charter fee.
Bring cash in Turkish lira for harbor-side teas, ice cream, or crew gratuities.

body.text: How far is Adrasan from Antalya Airport?

Adrasan lies roughly 100 to 105 km southwest of Antalya Airport (AYT), a drive of 1 hour 40 minutes to 2 hours depending on Antalya ring-road traffic ([Rome2Rio Antalya Airport to Adrasan](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Antalya-Airport-AYT/Adrasan)). Private transfers or rental cars follow the D400 coastal highway past Kemer and Çamyuva before turning off through forested hills to the bay.

Public transit requires extra time and transfers, as no direct airport bus serves Adrasan. Travelers without a car take a tram or municipal bus to Antalya Otogar (bus terminal), board an hourly Batı Antalya Tur minibus toward Kumluca along the D400, and transfer at the Adrasan junction to a local dolmuş or taxi—typically totaling 3.5 to 4 hours ([SooTransfer Adrasan Guide](https://www.sootransfer.com/en/adrasan/)). For short coastal stays, renting a car at AYT or pre-arranging a direct driver saves half a travel day and makes side trips to Olympos, Phaselis, and Demre straightforward.

faq.q: How long is the boat ride from Adrasan Harbor to Suluada?
faq.a: The crossing from Adrasan Harbor to Suluada takes roughly 40 to 50 minutes each way in calm morning seas, depending on the vessel's engine speed and swell conditions near Cape Gelidonya.

faq.q: Can you stay overnight on Suluada Island?
faq.a: No. Suluada is an uninhabited, protected volcanic island with no hotels, restaurants, restrooms, or overnight camping facilities. All visitors return to Adrasan or nearby mainland harbors by late afternoon.

faq.q: Is Adrasan Beach sandy or pebbly?
faq.a: Adrasan Beach is a mix of coarse sand and fine pebbles that slopes gently into clear, sheltered water. It is easier on bare feet than the larger stones at Olympos or Çıralı.

faq.q: Can you visit Olympos and Suluada on the same day?
faq.a: Doing both in one day is rushed because Suluada boat tours last six to seven hours. Spend one full day on the water and dedicate a separate morning or late afternoon to Olympos ruins and Yanartaş.

faq.q: Are there ATMs and pharmacies in Adrasan?
faq.a: Adrasan has basic village markets, seasonal cafés, and limited ATM access, though cash machines occasionally run dry in peak summer. Larger supermarkets, banks, and full-service pharmacies sit 20 minutes away in Kumluca.

faq.q: Is Suluada suitable for young children or non-swimmers?
faq.a: Yes, provided you choose a calm morning and a boat with proper life jackets and a sturdy rear swim ladder. Suluada's shallow shoreline lets children wade safely when anchorages are not crowded.
